paragraphs: TOML is a text format for configuration files. Its website provides specifications in several languages. On October 23, 2026, doggy8088 (Will, whose Facebook page is named Will 保哥的技術交流中心) proposed a Taiwanese Traditional Chinese locale and submitted a homepage, two specification versions and interface changes.

Project member arp242 characterized the first issue as an LLM prompt and objected to agent-mediated submissions. The issue and PR were closed. The contributor disclosed AI assistance, said he reviewed the work and accepted responsibility, and asked for assessment of the result. Two days later, a renewed issue was closed and locked after the maintainer linked Facebook.

Responses do not form a single camp: some emphasize human review and cultural differences, some criticize the submission or publicity strategy, and others also ask maintainers for better feedback. This chronicle paraphrases each statement and distinguishes participant claims from facts the record can establish.

status.label: At the capture cutoffs
status.title: All three threads are closed. The translation PR is unmerged.
paragraph: #97 and #99 were closed as not planned; #99 also restricts comments to collaborators. This chronicle has not comprehensively reviewed the meaning of both translations. AI use alone is not used to determine whether they pass or fail.

maintainerBackground.title: Who is arp242? Maintenance work and earlier positions

sections.title: A developer with a long record in Go and technical communities
paragraphs: arp242 publicly identifies as Martin Tournoij; his GitHub profile and personal website link to each other. His public CV describes him as the founder of GoatCounter, an open-source web analytics service focused on privacy and ease of use. NLnet separately records funding for the project between 2019 and 2022.

His public work also includes the Unicode lookup tool uni, the Go plugin gopher.vim and maintenance activity on Go libraries including fsnotify and lib/pq. His 2019 resignation post records that he served as a moderator on Vi and Vim Stack Exchange.

sections.title: Visible work in TOML
paragraphs: arp242 published the TOML 1.1.0 GitHub release, merged the Simplified Chinese and French 1.1.0 translations on toml.io and proposed a CODEOWNERS file to identify translation reviewers. That proposal remained unmerged when checked. These actions establish a maintenance role, but the public record alone does not show whether other members were consulted about the present decision.

sections.title: AI contribution bans predate this translation dispute
paragraphs: On August 19, 2026, Taiwan time, he added AI contribution policies to BurntSushi/toml, lib/pq and GoatCounter. They prohibit AI-generated PRs, issues, commit messages and comments. The restrictions cover several forms of contribution text; they cannot be reduced to a ban only on drafts lacking human review.

That day, he described roughly 110 agent reports and a large PR on lib/pq as difficult to review; the count and attribution are his account. The Go vulnerability database’s rolandshoemaker subsequently acknowledged that some reports had slipped through review, said they had been withdrawn and apologized. arp242 also said some issues could still be fixed. This gives context for his discussion of maintenance workload without establishing that all reports were fabricated.

sections.title: The fsnotify dispute over maintenance access
paragraphs: In May 2026, removing some collaborators’ access to fsnotify prompted public discussion. arp242 cited rapidly merged changes, inadequate quality and an undiscussed funding-list change. mattn listed fixes and releases, disputed the wholesale dismissal of his work and apologized for incorrectly describing the original maintainers as recently removed and for his judgment in directly changing the funding file. arp242 also acknowledged that he should have opened an issue beforehand. Quality and governance remained disputed; this provides context about maintenance procedures, not proof of his motive in rejecting the translation.

sections.title: Earlier views and the acceptance criteria still unresolved
paragraphs: In “Open source DIY ethics,” he describes open source as working together to solve problems and expects users to share the work. In “Tired of Stack Overflow,” he criticizes harsh treatment of newcomers and argues that quality and kindness can coexist. These are his earlier published views, not established explanations for his present replies.

The PR-base README provides translation steps but contains no AI clause. Policies in other projects do not automatically establish a previously announced toml.io rule. In the Russian discussion, pradyunsg described a practice of finding another native speaker to review. In #99, arp242 said he did not oppose Traditional Chinese, yet also said subsequent zh-TW submissions would be suspected of AI translation. Whether human checking and independent native-speaker review offer an acceptable path remains unanswered in the public record.
